title: Liverleaf
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Middle schooler Haruka Nozaki moves with her family to an isolated, snowbound rural town, where classmates turn on her and the teachers look away. After the bullies set a fire that kills her parents and leaves her younger sister badly hurt, Haruka takes bloody revenge. A short three-volume horror tragedy by the creator of Hi Score Girl.
life_message: Shows no good life so much as the ruin cruelty and indifference bring; love for family and one loyal friend are the only warmth.

content.note: Arson killing a family; bullies die gory deaths by scissors and nails (review; AniList Gore, MU Blood and Gore, Murder/s).
Relentless bullying, grief and dread; AniList Tragedy, Denpa; review calls it bleak, cruel and extremely tragic.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Haruka answers her tormentors personally with lethal force; teachers and rules fail.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Story celebrates neither order nor freedom; the closed town simply devours.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Haruka's loyalty is to family; the town turns on an outsider.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Neither tradition nor reason guides the town; not a theme.

folkways.japan: The closed rural school and teachers avoiding trouble before the school closes reflect Japanese concerns about ijime and group conformity against a transfer student.

delivery.evidence: Review notes cathartic revenge and exaggeration for effect, not a stated moral; no reviewer calls it preachy.
delivery.note: The story shows cruelty and revenge without characters arguing a worldview; the bullies are cruel individuals rather than voices for an idea.

winners_losers: Nearly everyone loses; the bullies die and Haruka is destroyed by grief and violence. Sympathy goes to Haruka and her family.
